sources.title: Electron capture and excitation in intermediate-energy He2+–H(1s,2s) collisions
sources.claim: Semiclassical straight-line AOCC uses a projectile ETF and an overlap matrix in coefficient propagation.
limits: Trajectory R=b+vt; active electron; atomic units in source.
Eq. (6) names S and M but does not supply all channel-dependent matrix elements required for an independent implementation.
Not a specification of finite-R molecular-orbital ETF switching.

sources.title: The dependence of nonadiabatic couplings on the origin of electron coordinates
sources.claim: Origin dependence of individual NACs cancels in the consistently transformed complete quantum nuclear equations, including mixed and second derivatives.
limits: Three particles with two heavy nuclei and one light particle; Jacobi reduced masses M and m.
Correct asymptotic channel construction and detailed ETF remedies are explicitly outside this paper.
Printed Eq. (13) omits the explicit m/hbar^2 factor visible in Eq. (16); use the chain rule Eq. (12) and dimensional Eq. (16) for provenance, not Eq. (13) alone.

sources.title: Isotope effects on the charge transfer into the n=1 , 2, and 3 shells of He2+ in collisions with H, D, and T
equations: unnumbered TD variational action and asymptotic overlap probability
sources.claim: END couples quantum AO electronic motion to classical nuclear trajectories determined with instantaneous electronic coupling; AOs carry ETFs and asymptotic final-state projection uses overlap information.
limits: No complete coefficient-equation specification is printed here; preceding END references are required for implementation.
The primary probability definition is the modulus-square of the final-state overlap; the following shorthand coefficient expression must not be copied without this operation.

sources.title: Hyperspherical close-coupling calculations for charge-transfer cross sections in He2++H(1s) collisions at low energies
sources.claim: Asymptotic atomic ETF prescription does not uniquely determine finite-separation MO switching; HSCC gives a separate quantum three-body route.
limits: Introductory methodological comparison, not proof that every ETF calculation is invalid.
HSCC hyperradius is not internuclear distance; coordinate meanings must remain distinct.
A coordinate-covariant semiclassical transport identity alone does not establish equivalence to quantum-nuclear HSCC.

sources.title: ARSENY: A program for computing inelastic transitions via hidden crossings in one-electron atomic ion–ion collisions with classical description of nuclear motion
sources.claim: ARSENY treats small-R rotational transitions through a 2l+1 electronic amplitude equation and assembles hidden-crossing transition probability matrices.
limits: Its x axis is internuclear and z axis normal to collision plane; Eq. (47) plus omega Lz sign is convention-specific.
Restricted small-R same-N,l rotational approximation; not general finite-R MO ETF transport.
Eq. (50) is a product of probability matrices, not a coherent amplitude propagator.

sources.title: Surface hopping, electron translation factors, electron rotation factors, momentum conservation, and size consistency
sources.claim: ETF/ERF surface-hopping corrections have explicit perturbative and conservation assumptions.
limits: Section III.A discards ETF-induced nonorthonormality and interatomic phase differences and keeps first-order velocity.
Section IV.B restricts exact rotated basis argument to rigid rotations.
Section VI excludes external fields and spin-orbit complications.
The written inverse of Lambda in Eqs. (96)–(97) is not directly available for a centered diatomic geometry. Last statement is our rank inference, not a quoted paper result.
